Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

The opponent has a Gideon of the Trials emblem preventing them from losing while they control a Gideon planeswalker, so I need to find a way to remove that planeswalker before attempting lethal damage—I'm considering whether Ayli's sacrifice ability can target it.

That ability requires 10 more life than starting total, meaning I'd need 30 life and I'm currently at 21, so I need to find 9+ life gain somewhere. Looking at the board, I'm counting blockers—Bruna at 5/7 flying vigilance and two Renegade Ralliers at 3/2—against my own creatures like Ayli, a lifelink Vampire Cutthroat, and Indulgent Aristocrat, trying to figure out if I can push through enough damage or need another angle entirely.

I'm mapping out my hand and mana: Angel of Invention with fabricate for extra bodies or pump, Sacred Cat, Stasis Snare, and Declaration in Stone, against my 10 lands split evenly between black and white sources. My plan is to gain life up to 30 using lifelink damage and Ayli's sacrifice-for-life ability, then use her exile ability on Gideon before swinging for lethal, though I need to work out the exact sequencing between combat damage and activating abilities in the right phase.

Actually the emblem only stops them from losing while Gideon's under their control, so if I deal enough combat damage to drop them to zero or below before removing Gideon, exiling him afterward triggers the state-based loss since their life total never resets. So the real plan is: attack for lethal damage this turn, gain life back through lifelink, then use Ayli post-combat to exile Gideon and let the state-based action finish them off — now I just need to work out if 10 mana covers casting Angel of Invention and everything else needed.

I'm weighing whether to fabricate the Angel into a 4/3 flying vigilance lifelink with counters, or split it into a 2/1 flier plus two 2/2 servos once the anthem effect applies, and tallying how that affects total attacking power against their blockers.

Since Gideon isn't a creature, it can't block, so I'm focusing on Bruna and the two Ralliers as the only obstacles, and realizing Vampire Cutthroat's skulk ability means its power must stay below all their blockers' power to slip through unblocked. With Cutthroat at 2/2, none of their creatures (5 and 3 power) can legally block it, opening a path for guaranteed lifelink damage.

Now I'm tallying total potential damage across Angel, Cutthroat, Aristocrat, and the two Sacred Cats versus their three blockers, checking whether we can force through the required 3 damage to the opponent while also hitting 9 life gained even after they assign blocks optimally.

Since all attackers deal their full damage regardless of blocks, total lifelink gain is 12, bringing life to 33, well past the 30 threshold. Checking mana costs, Angel plus Sacred Cat covers 6, leaving enough for Ayli's activation, and there should be extra creatures available to sacrifice.

Working through combat deaths: the Angel dies to Bruna's block, which strips the anthem effect and causes the surviving Sacred Cats to also die from now-lethal damage, but I still need something left over to sacrifice to Ayli after combat—likely the unblocked Cutthroat survives to serve that purpose.

After combat, I sacrifice a surviving creature to Ayli's activated ability, exiling Gideon of the Trials for {1}{W}{B}, which removes the emblem's protection so state-based actions check the opponent's negative life total and they lose. I need to double check whether I actually have the 30 life required to activate Ayli's ability in the first place, since it needs 10 more than the starting total.

Checking blocking scenarios: no matter how the opponent blocks, total lifelink damage from all my attackers sums to 12, since damage isn't prevented and there's nothing that changes this outcome regardless of which creatures block.

I'm also confirming Cutthroat's skulk ability means it can't be blocked by any of the opponent's creatures since they all have power 3 or higher, guaranteeing that damage gets through.

But then I realize Ayli shouldn't attack at all — if blocked by Bruna, Ayli would take 5 damage and die, and I need Ayli alive to use her sacrifice ability, so she stays back on defense.

I also need to keep a spare creature to sacrifice besides Ayli, so Cutthroat, being unblockable, should attack rather than sit back — otherwise the guaranteed unblocked attacker might just be a Cat dealing only 2 damage, which isn't lethal.

Cutthroat is unblockable anyway, so that's fine. Checking mana: casting the second Sacred Cat for one white, the Angel for five, leaving enough for Ayli's activation with a Plains, Swamp, and one to spare — it all works out with a land left over. I don't think Declaration in Stone is needed here.

Now I need to decide on Fabricate 2: counters versus Servos. With counters, the Angel becomes a 4/3 flier with lifelink since it doesn't buff itself. With Servos instead, the Angel stays 2/1 but I get two 2/2 tokens, giving more total power (6 versus 4) and more bodies to work with — that seems like the stronger choice.

Double-checking edge cases: Bruna has no relevant trigger, Ayli's damage prevention doesn't matter since it doesn't attack. Confirming skulk works for Cutthroat since all potential blockers have power greater than its boosted power of 2, with blockers at 5, 3, and 3.

Considering whether other spells like Stasis Snare are needed—they aren't, mana's tight anyway. Verifying that once Gideon is exiled and no Gideon planeswalker remains, the emblem's effect ends, and the opponent loses to state-based actions at 0 or less life per rule 104.3b.

Confirming the "can't lose the game" prevention only lasts until end of turn, so once it expires the opponent at negative life loses at the next check—also noting Gideon of the Trials' static ability only makes him a creature on his own turn, which doesn't matter here.

Now I'm sequencing the plan: main phase one, cast Sacred Cat and Angel of Invention with two +1/+1 counters via fabricate; attack with Angel, Cutthroat, Aristocrat, and both cats to push life to 33 or more; then in second main phase, pay {1}{W}{B} and sacrifice a surviving creature.

I want to double check that sacrificing Vampire Cutthroat works fine as Ayli's cost regardless of combat outcome, and that exiling Gideon of the Trials is legal since he's a nonland permanent with no hexproof or protection. I'm also weighing whether the second Sacred Cat is actually necessary for the damage math or if the attack total works without it.

Life total ends at 33. If Bruna blocks and kills the Angel, the +1/+1 buff disappears too, so the Sacred Cats blocked by Ralliers die regardless since they're already at lethal damage as 1/1s, while the unblocked Cutthroat and Aristocrat survive fine — the embalm ability on the Cats isn't needed here either way.

Life is guaranteed regardless of blocks: every attacker deals its damage to *something*, and all five attackers have lifelink: 4 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 12 → 33 life.
